answer.answer: Northstar did not remove policy checks; they were renamed. The Northstar 4 migration guide states that Northstar 4 renames policy checks to release guards and that their purpose is unchanged (northstar-policy-new). Historically, Northstar 3 called pre-deployment controls policy checks (northstar-policy-old). Both snapshots belong to the same subject lineage (subject_id northstar, lineage_id northstar-policy-doc), so the newer snapshot supersedes the older terminology. No source indicates removal of the controls themselves; the documented change is a rename with unchanged purpose. The only open point is that the sources do not enumerate whether any specific individual checks or rules were dropped alongside the rename.
current_truths: In Northstar 4, the pre-deployment controls formerly called policy checks are named 'release guards' [northstar-policy-new]
The purpose of these controls is unchanged in Northstar 4 despite the rename [northstar-policy-new]
historical_truths: In Northstar 3, pre-deployment controls were called 'policy checks' [northstar-policy-old]
unresolved: The sources do not state whether any specific individual policy checks or rules were removed or altered beyond the rename; only the naming change and unchanged purpose are documented [northstar-policy-new]
